the development and characterization of a model of mammary tumor development.
the identification and characterization of the cell types that comprise the mammary tumor.
the characterization and cloning of the various cell types that constitute the mouse mammary adenocarcinomalike tumor.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three cell lines represent different stages of mammary cell differentiation.

we have established a series of cell lines that are clonally related and represent the three major cell types that have been observed in the original tumor and in the tumors that arise from these lines.
the three major cell types in these mammary tumor cell lines represent three different developmental pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mammary tumor cell lines can be established from transplanted tumors that have a variety of morphological, functional, and genetic features.

the three major cell types in the mouse mammary tumor cell lines are developmentally related and that the tumorigenic potential of the cell types is inversely related to their degree of epithelial differentiation.
the cell lines we have isolated are not homogeneous and that there are multiple pathways of progression from the polygonal to the cuboidal and to the elongated cells.
